input.prompt: A single vintage 1970s ceramic EPROM chip in a long, deep dual in-line package, seen straight on from the front, perfectly horizontal and flat, centred, filling the width; the body's height is about a third of its length. The ceramic body is burnt terracotta orange enamel with a fine matte grain and a thin gold seal ring. LEFT END: one flat empty square gold plate, blank, in the upper half only; below it a smooth bare stretch of burnt terracotta orange ceramic, blank. Between the gold plate and the label: one SQUARE quartz glass window with slightly rounded corners, set flush in a thin gold frame, as tall as the label panel, through it a dark empty black cavity, completely blank. RIGHT HALF: one large flat empty rectangular label panel of matte black epoxy with a very fine grain and a thin gold border, blank, taking the whole right half of the body and nearly its full height. Gold legs along the top and bottom edges. Painted light: one strong warm golden key light from behind the chip casting broad golden rays upward, like a halo; a green rim light on the left edge, a red rim light on the right edge. Painted comic book illustration in exactly the style of the reference image (the green NVIDIA chip): a real object drawn sharp with clean black ink outlines on every part, comic halftone dots only inside the shadows, saturated colour. The object alone on a pure black void, seen clearly. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no symbols, no flags, no signs, no markings anywhere.
